CheckTitle: Bedrock AgentCore browser tool has session recording enabled
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis
Description: The **Bedrock AgentCore browser tool** can record agent browsing sessions to S3 for later review. This check verifies `recording.enabled` is `true` on each browser resource.
Risk: A **browser tool** without session recording (`recording.enabled` not `true`) leaves no forensic record of the pages an agent visited or the actions it took during a browsing session, hindering incident investigation if the agent is manipulated into unsafe browsing behavior.

Code.NativeIaC:
```yaml
Resources:
  example_resource:
    Type: AWS::BedrockAgentCore::BrowserCustom
    Properties:
      Name: example_resource
      RecordingConfig:
        Enabled: true  # Critical: enables session recording
        S3Location:
          Bucket: example-bucket
          Prefix: agentcore-browser/
```
Code.Other:
1. Open the AWS Console and go to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
2. Select **Tools**, then the browser tool
3. Edit its recording configuration
4. Enable recording and choose an S3 destination
5. Save the browser tool

Recommendation.Text: Enable session recording on every Bedrock AgentCore browser tool and direct it to an S3 bucket, so browsing sessions are available for forensic review after an incident.

Notes: This check reports one finding per browser resource discovered via ListBrowsers/GetBrowser in each scanned region. A browser whose GetBrowser detail could not be retrieved returns MANUAL rather than PASS or FAIL, because an absent recording block means the answer is unknown, not that recording is disabled.
